title: Resilience-First SKU Architectures and SLA Bundles for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Define a new set of Dedicated capacity SKUs and accompanying SLA bundles that prioritize availability/resilience for enterprise customers with predictable pricing. The goal is to offer a 'resilience-first' product line that makes trade-offs between reserved GPU commitments, burst credits, autoscale behavior, and contractual SLOs explicit and easy to sell. This ticket scopes SKU definitions, pricing heuristics, contract language for common security questionnaire asks (network isolation, KMS, audit logs), and an internal checklist for Sales/SE quoting.
acceptance_criteria: A matrix of 4 SKU tiers (Resilience Basic / Resilience Plus / Resilience Premium / Resilience Ultra) with clear resource units (vGPU-equivalent), burst credit allocations, and autoscale delta is documented
Each SKU has a defined SLA bundle tied to an uptime SLO, restart MTTR target, and economic remediation (credit formula) for misses
Pricing model for reserved commit, monthly billing, and overage/burst accounting is provided as a simple spreadsheet and unit pricing rules
Contract language snippets for top 10 security questionnaire items are drafted and reviewed by Security
Sales quoting template populated with examples for three reference customer profiles (startup, mid-market, regulated enterprise)
tasks: Draft SKU matrix: resource units, burst credits, baseline throughput guarantees
Design autoscale policies per SKU: scale-up thresholds, guaranteed warm capacity, max burst duration
Work with Pricing to convert resource units into MSRP and discount ladders for annual commit
Coordinate with Security to produce approved answers for common questionnaire items (VPC, KMS, audit logs, data retention)
Create SLA terms and credit formulas and run legal review for inclusion in contract addendum
Build an internal quoting sheet and sample SOW language for Sales/SE
Run a risk trade-off doc comparing cost-per-availability vs cost-per-throughput across SKUs
Prepare rollout FAQ and enablement slide deck for GTM

decisions: Adopt RU (resource unit) abstraction to decouple SKU names from hardware generation. RU maps to an internal GPU-hour equivalent documented in the pricing sheet.
Burst credits will be time-boxed and measured in RU-minutes; unused burst credits do not roll over monthly for Standard SKUs but roll over for Annual Ultra customers.
Autoscale warm capacity will be guaranteed as a percentage of reserved RU: Basic 20%, Plus 40%, Premium 60%, Ultra 80%.
SLA credit structure will be a sliding scale based on monthly uptime percentage with a maximum remediation cap equal to one month of reserved fees.
Security questionnaire answers will include a standard 'Customer Data Segregation' blurb and an optional appendix for on-prem/VPC deployments.

risks: Underpricing Premium RU could devalue Dedicated revenue and increase capacity pressure; mitigation: run market survey and alpha offers with 2 customers.
SLA credit caps could be seen as insufficient by regulated customers; mitigation: provide optional enterprise SLA with higher remediation tied to longer commits.
Autoscale warm guarantees require runtime changes to pre-warm KV caches which add engineering risk; mitigation: schedule a runbook and spike with ENG-40212.
